title: Task Stdout Streaming Foundation
goal: Expose live task output truthfully so active runs feel observable without inventing telemetry.
scope: Implement the first per-task stdout streaming slice through the existing task lifecycle. Add a bounded stream buffer, task stdout SSE endpoint, and terminal-style Mission Control panel only where runner output can be captured safely.
generation_reason: Product recommendation coverage audit found per-task stdout streaming was explicitly deferred but not queued as its own package.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Stream only real task output and preserve existing dispatch, approval, and runtime binding paths. Do not add a second runner protocol.
notes: Output buffers must be bounded and safe for secrets.
Terminal UI must clearly show unavailable output when a runner cannot stream.

success_criteria: At least one supported runner path can emit bounded stdout lines tied to task identity.
A task stdout stream endpoint exposes only authorized, sanitized task output.
Mission Control can render a truthful terminal panel for streaming and unavailable states.
Tests cover streaming, completion, missing task, and no-stream fallback behavior.
Existing approval, dispatch, pack binding, and evidence paths remain intact.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Stdout stream content is real, bounded, and tied to task identity.
No approval, dispatch, or runtime binding bypass is introduced.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
Runner output safety and secret redaction constraints are reviewed before implementation.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with stdout streaming changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the stdout streaming baseline and remaining runner limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
